announcementAdmin.collapseHint: Off by default: every announcement is shown in full. Turn it on to show only the first and fold the rest behind a “N more” link.
announcementAdmin.crowded: {{count}} announcements are live at once. Readers will not get through that many — consider merging some, giving the older ones an end time, or switching a few off.
announcementAdmin.grantsRequired: Pick at least one recipient, or nobody will see this announcement
announcementAdmin.grantsTruncated: Only the first {{count}} accounts are listed. To reach others, put them in a group.
announcementAdmin.hint: Drag to set the order readers see. Each row saves on its own — there is no page-level Save.
announcementAdmin.popupSkippedHint: At most one popup per page load, and only the topmost one gets it.
announcementAdmin.previewEmpty: This recipient currently sees no announcements
announcementAdmin.scopeHint: "Home only" is the original behaviour — a full card on the home page. "Every page" adds a collapsed strip at the top of every page behind the login, which expands when clicked. Neither shows in the admin console or on mobile chat.
announcementAdmin.staleHint: This announcement has no end time and has been showing for a while. Is it still needed?
announcementAdmin.unreachableHint: This announcement is addressed to chosen recipients, but none of them exist any more — usually because the group it named was deleted. Nobody is receiving it. Pick recipients again, switch it to Everyone, or turn it off.
announcementAdmin.windowHint: Picked in your own timezone. Leave empty to start now and never end automatically. Setting an end time is what stops an incident banner from being forgotten.
apps.adminHint: Upload a .zip bundle (an app.json manifest + a self-contained index.html). Apps run in a sandboxed iframe and reach the API only through a scoped bridge. See docs/adr/0003-downloadable-apps.md.
apps.batchDesc: Run a workflow over many rows — see per-row results and re-run failures
apps.marketEmpty: The market has no apps to install yet.
apps.marketHint: One-click install community apps from the GitHub app market, or install manually by uploading a .zip bundle above.
apps.permNone: This app requests no data access.

audit.f.name: name
audit.geoActiveHint: Leave on automatic to use whichever database was updated most recently.
audit.geoAttribution: Attribution is required wherever the data is shown: MaxMind (GeoLite2), DB-IP, or IPinfo, depending on which database you use.
audit.geoDownloadHint: “Download now” saves these settings first, then downloads.
audit.geoEditionHint: Blank means {{def}}. A paid account can name another edition.
audit.geoEulaHint: “Download now” saves these settings first, then fetches. MaxMind's licence requires the data to be refreshed at least every 30 days, so leaving auto-update on is the safer choice.
audit.geoIntervalHint: hours between checks (minimum 1; takes effect without a restart)
audit.geoKeyHint: Write-only; never shown again once saved.
audit.geoKeySaved: Saved — leave blank to keep it
audit.geoMissing: No IP database. Put a MaxMind-format .mmdb in {{dir}} to show where an address is; it is read locally and no address is ever sent anywhere.
audit.geoMissingShort: No IP database installed — configure one under Settings → General to show where an address is.
audit.geoOff: IP locations are switched off (Settings → General).
audit.geoOfflineHint: Resolved from a local .mmdb — no third-party lookups, so no visitor's address is ever sent anywhere. Drop a database into {{dir}}, or configure a download below. Country and region are reliable; city is approximate.
audit.geoSrcDbip: DB-IP City Lite (city-level, no account needed)
audit.geoSrcIpinfo: IPinfo Lite (country + ASN only, token required)
audit.geoSrcMaxmind: MaxMind GeoLite2 (city-level, free licence key required)
audit.intro: Who read which report, and who changed who may read it. Retention is configured under Storage — leave the audit target off and nothing is ever deleted.
audit.legacyTimeHint: Recorded before v0.4.15, when stamps were the server's local clock with no timezone written down. There is no honest way to convert it, so it is shown as stored.
audit.proxyHintBody: Requests are arriving with an X-Forwarded-For header from a peer that is not listed in trusted_proxies, so the portal will not believe it — otherwise anyone could claim any address. Add the proxy's address or subnet to trusted_proxies in config.yaml and restart; addresses recorded before that stay as they are.
audit.proxyHintTitle: These addresses are your reverse proxy, not your visitors
audit.title: Audit log
batch.admin.advancedPluginsHint: Import a manifest to run a non-Dify provider. Most setups only need Dify targets above.
batch.admin.ageHoursHint: Wait time at which the age factor reaches its max (1).
batch.admin.defaultPriorityHint: Base priority (0–100) for a run whose submitter is in no group with a default. Urgent runs still require a ticket.
batch.admin.difyEndUserHint: The `user` Dify records for each run. Use [username] for the submitting portal user, e.g. [username]@anchan.kazuha.org. Blank = report-portal.
batch.admin.difyPollHint: 0 = keep the streaming connection open until the run finishes. Set >0 to instead grab the run id then poll its status every N seconds — avoids a long-held stream through a proxy.
batch.admin.difyRunTimeoutHint: Max time to wait/poll for one run before giving up. Must exceed your longest workflow — a run cut short is wrongly marked failed. Default 180.
batch.admin.fairHalflifeHint: A user's recent runs decay by half over this window.
batch.admin.maxJobsHint: How many runs execute at once across the whole queue — a single analysis, or each row of a batch, is one run. 1 = one at a time, in priority order.
batch.admin.presetsHint: Users can pick one of these when running; the run is scheduled into that window.
batch.admin.prioWeightsHint: A queued run's score = w_base·base + w_age·age + w_fair·fair (each factor 0–1). Higher weight makes that factor matter more; 0 disables it.
batch.admin.reservedSlotsHint: Slots kept for urgent jobs so they always have a lane (capped below the max).
batch.admin.runDefaultsMoved: The run form’s defaults (default workflow, default mode, default preset window…) are set here:
batch.admin.surfacesAgentHint: Chat apps produce no report, so they cannot be used in Run analysis / Batch.
batch.admin.surfacesHint: Where this target can be picked. Unticked surfaces hide it entirely.
batch.admin.surfacesWorkflowHint: Workflow apps are not conversational, so they cannot be used in the Assistant.
batch.admin.ticketPeriodHint: How often each user's urgent tickets refill.
batch.admin.urgentEnabledHint: Off by default. When off, the urgent lane is hidden everywhere and any urgent submit runs at its base priority.
batch.admin.wBaseHint: Weight of the configured base priority.
batch.admin.wFairHint: Weight of fair-share — heavy recent users yield to lighter ones.
batch.csvPlaceholder: Paste CSV; first row is the header: {{keys}}
batch.dify.apiKeyHint: The app-… service key of the workflow to run. One key per workflow.
batch.dify.apiKeyKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the current key. Paste a new key to replace it.
batch.dify.apiKeyKeepPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the current key
batch.dify.baseUrlHint: e.g. https://your-dify/v1 — the service API base, ending in /v1.
batch.dify.chatHint: This is a chat / agent app — each row's `query` column is the message it runs.
batch.dify.connectedNoInputs: Connected to "{{name}}", but inputs could not be read. Add them manually below.
batch.dify.inputsManual: Inputs could not be read automatically — add them manually.
batch.dify.noInputs: No inputs — add at least one.
batch.dify.outputSubtypeHint: The report subtype this workflow generates. Required for external groups: it decides what they may see, and lets an existing same-day report be reused instead of running again.
batch.dify.symbolInputHint: Which input carries the stock code. Set it together with the report type to enable same-day reuse; left empty, this workflow always runs.
batch.dify.targetsHint: No targets yet. Add a Dify workflow with its API key and its inputs are discovered automatically.
batch.noTargets: No runnable targets yet. Ask an admin to configure a target under Manage → Batch jobs.
batch.refresh.inputsUnavailable: Connected, but the parameter list did not answer — its parameters are left alone.
batch.refresh.noChanges: Every target's parameters already match Dify.
batch.refresh.scopeHint: Only the parameter list and the app kind are written. The target name, report type, stock-code input, address and key are left as they are.
batch.refresh.symbolLost: The stock-code input {{name}} is gone from the parameter list. Applying this turns off same-day reuse until another one is chosen.
batch.refresh.title: Pull updates from Dify
batch.status.untrackedHint: The run was dispatched to Dify but left no trackable handle, so its final outcome can't be confirmed. It was not re-run, to avoid a duplicate charged run. If a run handle was kept, you can reconcile it manually later.
batch.ticketDowngraded: Out of urgent tickets — ran as normal
captcha.providerUnsupported: This portal is configured to use a hosted captcha provider, which this build does not embed. Ask an administrator to switch to the built-in image captcha.
chat.busy: The assistant is busy — too many chats in progress. Try again in a moment.
chat.deleteConfirm: Delete this conversation? Dify keeps the messages.
chat.enterHint: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a newline
chat.noTargets: No chat or agent apps yet. Add one under Manage → Targets (a Dify chat/agent app).
chat.stillRunning: Still generating — this can take a while; it updates when it finishes.
chatAdmin.convsHint: Read-only oversight of every user’s assistant chats.
chatAdmin.limitHint: Across all users; over this, new turns are asked to retry. 0 = unlimited. Chat is interactive and runs independently of the run queue.
chatAdmin.streamHint: Off: the reply returns all at once (fallback if streaming misbehaves behind a proxy).
chatAdmin.turnTimeoutHint: Longest one reply may run before the live stream gives up — raise it for long agent / deep-research replies (it also bounds how long the browser recovers the answer after a dropped connection). Behind a reverse proxy, raise nginx proxy_read_timeout to match.

login.forgotSent: If that account exists, a reset link is on its way — check your email.
login.ssoFailed: Single sign-on did not complete ({{reason}}). Use the username and password form instead, or ask an administrator to check the identity provider.
login.ssoReason.bad_issuer: the response came from a different identity provider than the one configured
login.ssoReason.bad_response: the identity provider's response could not be read
login.ssoReason.bad_state: the sign-in did not match the request that started it; it may have been left open too long
login.ssoReason.bad_token: the identity provider's token could not be verified
login.ssoReason.exchange_failed: the portal could not exchange the code with the identity provider
login.ssoReason.idp_error: the identity provider refused the sign-in
login.ssoReason.internal: the portal hit an internal error
login.ssoReason.no_id_token: the identity provider returned no id token
login.ssoReason.not_provisioned: no account here matched that identity, and this provider did not create one; the server log names the reason
login.ssoReason.provider_unavailable: single sign-on is not usable right now; its configuration is incomplete or the identity provider is unreachable
login.ssoReason.saml_ambiguous_email: more than one account uses that email address, so the sign-in cannot choose between them
login.ssoReason.saml_assertion_rejected: the assertion failed verification — signature, audience or timing; the server log names which
login.ssoReason.saml_attributes: the assertion's attributes could not be read
login.ssoReason.saml_bad_subject: the identity provider's user identifier could not be used
login.ssoReason.saml_destination: the assertion was addressed to a different URL than this portal's; check the Reply URL registered at the identity provider
login.ssoReason.saml_encrypted: the assertion was encrypted, which this portal does not accept
login.ssoReason.saml_no_nameid: the identity provider sent no unique user identifier
login.ssoReason.saml_replay: that assertion had already been used
login.ssoReason.saml_transient_nameid: the identity provider sent a temporary user id that changes on every sign-in; its NameID format needs to be persistent, emailAddress or unspecified
login.ssoReason.saml_weak_signature: the assertion was signed with an algorithm this portal refuses
login.ssoReason.sso_no_email_claim: this provider is set to match accounts by email, but no email claim is mapped, so there is nothing to match on

preset.overrunHint: What to do with a run still waiting when the window closes; a run already in progress always finishes.

recurring.noTargets: No run targets yet — create one in the batch console first.

recurring.runNowBody: This fires the task immediately, without affecting its schedule.

reset.noToken: This reset link is missing its token.
reset.title: Set a new password
review.emptyBody: This page lists what your reports assumed and when each should be checked, so a judgement can be revisited instead of forgotten. The assumptions come from the workflow that writes the report — add a `tracking` array to the ingest call and they will appear here.
review.emptyHint: `itype` and `status` are free text (`status` defaults to pending). Put an ISO date in `review_point` and it becomes a real due date you can sort by; without one the item is ordered by age.
review.emptyTitle: No assumptions have been recorded yet
review.title: Assumption review
run.fileTooLarge: {{name}} is larger than {{mb}}MB and cannot be uploaded
run.noTargets: No workflows configured yet. Add one under Manage → Batch.
run.queueBusy: Queue full ({{n}} running) — {{ahead}} ahead of you, this will wait its turn.
run.reusedToday: This report was already generated today — opening it (no run used).
run.title: Run analysis
runDefaults.hint: What the Run analysis dialog opens on. These are pre-filled suggestions — the user can change any of them in the form, and each one can be left unset.
runDefaults.modeHint: Which button the run dialog opens on.
runDefaults.notifyHint: Only takes effect for a user with a verified address on a portal that can send mail.
runDefaults.presetHint: Pre-picked in Preset mode. A window that is switched off is never offered in the run form.
runDefaults.retriesHint: How many times a failed run retries by itself (0–5). Default 0: one click, one run.
runDefaults.showRuleHint: On, the run form prints a window’s whole rule after its name; off, it shows the name and keeps the rule behind the button beside it.
runDefaults.title: Run form defaults
runDefaults.workflowHint: Pre-selected when the dialog opens. An entry button that names its own workflow still wins.
security.apiRateHint: Calls to /api/v1 allowed per minute from one source; above it the answer is 429. 0 means no ceiling, which is the default. Check what your integrations call at before changing it.
security.captchaDesc: Raises the cost of each automated attempt on the public forms. It complements the rate limit rather than replacing it — the limit bounds how fast one source can try, the captcha bounds how cheaply many sources can.
security.limitsDesc: How long being signed in lasts, and how often one source may knock.
security.loginFailMaxHint: Failures from one IP or against one account within the window before further attempts are refused. A correct password always passes, so the account owner is never locked out.
security.loginFailWindowHint: How long failures are counted for; the count clears once the window lapses.
security.loginModeHint: What the sign-in page offers. This is presentation only — what the server ACCEPTS is the switch below.
security.noProviderWarning: No identity provider is enabled, so these settings are currently inert: the sign-in page falls back to password only and password login is still accepted. Configure SAML or OIDC first.
security.onForgotHint: Aimed at using the portal to flood someone else’s inbox.
security.providerHint: The built-in image captcha needs no external service, which matters if this portal sits where Google and Cloudflare are unreachable.
security.regDesc: Lets visitors create their own account. Off by default.
security.regDomainsHint: Comma separated. Leave empty to accept any domain.
security.regGroupHint: Leave as “nobody yet” and a new account can sign in but see nothing until you place it. Choose an OU and it inherits that OU’s readable report versions immediately.
security.regGroupNone: Nobody yet — I will place them myself
security.regNeedsEmail: Email confirmation is on but SMTP is not configured, so registration will refuse rather than create accounts nobody can activate. Configure email first.
security.regVerifyHint: Strongly recommended — without it anyone can register using someone else’s address.
security.secretKeyHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave blank to keep the current one.
security.secretStored: A secret is stored — leave blank to keep it
security.sessionTTLHint: How long before signing in is needed again. Lowering it signs everyone out sooner; an SSO provider’s own session limit still applies, whichever is shorter.
security.ssoOnlyHint: Enforced by the server, whatever the page shows. Administrators are always exempt, so a broken identity provider can never lock you out of fixing it.
security.thresholdHint: Counted per address and per account within the lockout window; either reaching it turns the captcha on.
security.tokenProviderNote: Hosted providers need their script to load in the visitor’s browser. This build ships only the image captcha, so the public forms will explain that instead of showing a widget.
settings.announcementContentPlaceholder: Example: We have deployed a fix and are monitoring the situation. If access still fails, try switching to another node.
settings.announcementContentTooLong: Announcement content must be 2000 characters or fewer
settings.announcementTitlePlaceholder: Example: Some nodes had auth errors (fixed, monitoring)
settings.announcementTitleTooLong: Announcement title must be 160 characters or fewer
settings.footerTextHint: Supports safe lightweight HTML such as a, strong, and br. Blank = use the site title.
settings.footerTextTooLong: Footer info must be 1000 characters or fewer
settings.logoHint: Use an http(s) image URL, a site path starting with /, or upload a small image under 512KB. Uploaded files are saved as site file paths. Leave blank to use the default icon.
settings.logoReadFailed: Failed to read the logo file
settings.publicUrlHint: The address people reach this portal at, e.g. https://portal.example.com. Reset and confirmation links, the SSO redirect and ACS URLs, the passkey relying-party id and the captcha host check all derive from it — so a link cannot be poisoned by a forged Host header. An origin only: no path.
settings.publicUrlInvalid: Enter an origin like https://portal.example.com — no path.
settings.pwaIconHint: Use an http(s) image URL, a site path starting with /, or upload a small image under 512KB. Blank = follow the logo; if the logo is blank, use the default icon.
settings.siteTitleTooLong: Site title must be 80 characters or fewer
settings.timezoneHint: Sets the timezone for the server-side notion of "today" (date=today, /api/v1/now) and non-browser rendering (PDF/email). Blank = follow the system zone. Timestamps in the UI render in each viewer's own browser timezone; report trading dates are market dates, identical for everyone.
settings.tokenCreatedHint: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again.
sso.allowAdminRoleHint: Off by default. While off, a rule targeting an admin role is ignored rather than honoured.
sso.allowIdpInitiatedHint: Off by default: it disables the check that a response answers a request we issued.
sso.attrExternalIdHint: The provider's immutable object id. Set it now: it is what links an account to future automatic provisioning.
sso.attrGroupsHint: What the group rules match against.
sso.attrUpnHint: Used only to name a NEW account. Use "nameid" to read the SAML Subject.
sso.claimsHint: The names below are what this identity provider actually sent. Copy one into the matching field — providers disagree about these, and a wrong guess fails the sign-in with a message about accounts rather than about the mapping.
sso.claimsNoneYet: No sign-in has been recorded through this provider yet. Attempt one — even a failed one records the claim names, and this panel then tells you exactly what to put in the fields below.
sso.claimsTitle: Claims seen on the last sign-in
sso.defaultGroupHint: Where a new account lands. Choose an external group: it decides what they can see and run.
sso.enableHint: Turning this on validates the configuration first; a provider stays a draft until it can actually work.
sso.guide.needPublicUrl: Set the site's public URL under Settings → General first. Until it is set, the values below are relative paths, which no identity provider will accept.
sso.guide.oidc.step1: Register the application in your identity provider
sso.guide.oidc.step1.entra: Entra ID → App registrations → New registration, platform Web.
sso.guide.oidc.step1.google: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials → Create OAuth client ID → Web application.
sso.guide.oidc.step1.keycloak: Keycloak → your realm → Clients → Create client → client type OpenID Connect, with client authentication on.
sso.guide.oidc.step1.okta: Okta Admin → Applications → Create App Integration → OIDC, Web Application.
sso.guide.oidc.step1.other: Register a confidential OpenID Connect client using the authorization-code flow.
sso.guide.oidc.step2.body: The identity provider will refuse the sign-in unless this address is registered exactly as shown, character for character.
sso.guide.oidc.step3: Copy the issuer, client ID and secret back here
sso.guide.oidc.step3.body: The issuer is the base address the portal appends /.well-known/openid-configuration to; do not paste the discovery document's own URL. It usually looks like:
sso.guide.oidc.step4: Confirm the scopes and the claims
sso.guide.oidc.step4.body: openid profile email covers the usual case. If you map groups, request the scope that carries them and grant admin consent — a claim the identity provider never sends cannot be mapped here.
sso.guide.saml.metadataShortcut: The Entity ID above is also the portal's SAML metadata document. Most identity providers can read it directly — Entra's "Upload metadata file" accepts the URL and fills both boxes for you.
sso.guide.saml.step1: Create the application in your identity provider
sso.guide.saml.step1.entra: Entra ID → Enterprise applications → New application → Create your own application → then Single sign-on → SAML.
sso.guide.saml.step1.google: Google Admin → Apps → Web and mobile apps → Add app → Add custom SAML app.
sso.guide.saml.step1.keycloak: Keycloak → your realm → Clients → Create client → client type SAML.
sso.guide.saml.step1.okta: Okta Admin → Applications → Create App Integration → SAML 2.0.
sso.guide.saml.step2: Give the identity provider the portal's two addresses
sso.guide.saml.step2.body: These identify this portal and tell the identity provider where to send the signed assertion. They are derived from the site's public URL and must match exactly.
sso.guide.saml.step3: Check which attributes the assertion carries
sso.guide.saml.step3.body: The portal needs a stable user identifier, and can use an email, a display name and group names if they are sent. Entra sends its defaults (user.userprincipalname, user.mail, user.displayname) with no extra work; groups have to be added as a claim. Whatever names your identity provider uses, enter them in the attribute mapping below.
sso.guide.saml.step4: Bring the identity provider's metadata back here
sso.guide.saml.step4.body: Paste its metadata URL into the field below and use "Fetch metadata" — that is what supplies the signing certificate. Find it at:
sso.guide.step5.body: Sign out, then use the single sign-on button on the login page. If provisioning is off, the account must already exist in the portal and be linked — otherwise the sign-in is refused rather than creating a stranger an account.
sso.guide.title: Setup guide — what goes where
sso.iconHint: Shown beside the name on the login page. Built-in icons are drawn locally; an uploaded image is served by this portal. Neither makes a visitor's browser contact anyone else.
sso.issuerHint: Use your tenant's issuer, not a shared one.
sso.linkByHint: Choosing username or email says this identity provider is authoritative for those fields: whoever controls it can then sign in as any account they name. Correct for one company IdP, wrong for anything federated with the outside. An email shared by two accounts is refused rather than guessed.
sso.mappingHint: Which claim carries each value. Accounts are always linked by the provider's subject, never by email.
sso.matchHint: How a sign-in that has never been linked before finds an account that already exists. This is separate from creating one.
sso.metadataUrlHint: Fetched over https; a failed refresh keeps the last working copy.
sso.needPublicUrl: Set the Public URL in Manage → Email first: every redirect and callback address is derived from it.
sso.provisioningHint: With creation off, an unknown user is told to contact an administrator.
sso.redirectUrlHint: Paste this into your identity provider. It is derived from the Public URL and cannot be edited.
sso.rules.empty: No rules. Every federated login falls through to the provider's default role and OU.
sso.rules.intro: Rules decide the role and the organizational unit of a federated account, and the OU is what carries report visibility, the run allow-list and the daily quota. They are evaluated top to bottom and the first match wins — drag to reorder.
sso.rules.keepOnMissHint: When no rule matches, leave an existing account as it is instead of applying the provider defaults. A brand-new account never takes this path.
sso.rules.noProviders: No identity provider is configured yet, so no rule can ever fire. Set one up on the SAML or OIDC tab first.
sso.rules.orderHint: First match wins; drag rows to change the order.
sso.rules.shadowedHint: An earlier enabled rule already answers for this attribute and value, so this one can never win.
sso.secretKeepHint: A secret is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
sso.sessionHoursHint: 0 = the default 7 days. Shorter means a disabled account at the provider loses access sooner.
sso.spHint: These are derived from your Public URL. Paste them into your identity provider.
storage.auditHint: Off means entries are kept forever. When on, the minimum retention is {{n}} days.
storage.batchHint: Delete finished/cancelled runs older than the retention.
storage.cleaned: Cleaned {{batch}} batch jobs, {{reports}} reports, {{tokens}} tokens, {{audit}} audit entries.
storage.confirmBody: Permanently delete {{n}} {{cat}} older than {{days}} days. This cannot be undone.
storage.confirmReportsBody: {{count}} report(s) older than {{days}} days match and will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
storage.reportsWarn: Only reports with a real ingest timestamp older than the retention are removed; imported / date-only reports are always kept. Off by default.
storage.scheduleHint: Run the enabled targets automatically on this cadence.
storage.title: Cleanup & retention
storage.tokensHint: Delete tokens expired longer ago than the grace period.
types.label: Display name (tab)
types.reclassifyConfirm: Reclassify all stored reports by the current category mapping?
types.restoreDefaultsConfirm: Clear all current type config and restore the defaults auto-generated on first run? Custom types are removed; stored reports are unaffected (a type that still has reports stays on as uncategorized).
update.desc: The portal system was updated. Refresh to load the latest version.
users.dailyRunQuotaHint: The most runs each member may start in the window. 0 = unlimited. Administrators are exempt.
users.defaultGroupHint: Every user without an assigned group inherits these settings.
users.expiresHint: Leave empty for no expiry. After this date (panel timezone) the account can no longer sign in.
users.groupTargetsHint: Choose which workflows this OU may run and where they appear. Nothing selected means its members can run nothing.
users.maxQueuedHint: Most runs a member may have queued or running at once. 0 = unlimited. Admins are exempt.
users.parentOuHint: Sub-OUs inherit their parent’s settings — restriction, quota, run allow-list and readable report versions.
users.primaryGroupHint: Leave empty to inherit the Default group.
users.priorityHint: Base priority (0–100) a member's runs default to. Empty inherits the system default. Urgent runs are separate and require a ticket.
users.restrictedHint: Members may only read reports their own OU generated, plus today's internal reports. Applies to every sub-OU.
users.runWindowHint: Hours (panel time) when members may start runs, e.g. 9-18, or 22-6 to wrap midnight. Empty = any time. Admins are exempt.
users.unlinkConfirm: Revoke this account's {{slug}} binding? The account stays, returns to local sign-in and its sessions end — set a password if they should keep signing in.
users.urgentPolicyHint: Whether members may use the urgent lane, and whether it costs a ticket.
users.weightHint: How many urgent runs each member may make per period. 0 = none.
verify.failed: This confirmation link is invalid or has expired.
verify.missing: This link is missing its token.
verify.ok: Your account is active. You can sign in now.
versions.defaultHint: Reports ingested without a version land here.
versions.deleteConfirm: Remove this version? Reports already published in it are kept, but nobody will be able to read them until it is registered again.
versions.desc: A report can be published in several written forms — for example a full internal edition and a shorter external one. Each form is produced by its own run, so a report exists in whichever forms have actually been generated.
versions.grantsHint: Groups and accounts. Nobody selected means nobody can read this version.
versions.label: Display name
versions.name: Name
versions.nameHint: The stable id workflows send as "version". It cannot be changed later — rename the display name instead.
versions.title: Report versions
webhook.hint: On new reports or finished batch jobs, a signed event is POSTed to these URLs. Write the receiver in your own service (push to Feishu / send email / …).
webhook.required: URL and at least one event are required
webhook.secretHint: Optional. Used for the HMAC-SHA256 signature so subscribers can verify authenticity.
webhook.title: Event webhooks
